Introduction C.1.1 Background The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is responsible for ensuring that Air Traffic Control (ATC) specialists provide the flying public with a high level of safety and professionalism. A well-trained ATC workforce plays an essential role in fulfilling this responsibility. The FAA employs more than 14,000 air traffic controllers. They work in air traffic facilities of varying sizes, safely separating more than 50,000 aircraft in the National Airspace System (NAS) each day. To provide such air traffic services, the FAA trains new air traffic control specialists

forms_signatures.text: All training and instructional support services must be performed in accordance with FAA Order JO 3120.4S, Air Traffic Technical Training, and in accordance with other applicable FAA Orders, Directives, and Standards referenced in Section C.2.1. The Contractor must provide qualified instructors and training program support service staff to conduct and administer all tasks required under this SOW. All instructors and training support services staff must meet the minimum personnel qualifications listed in Attachment J-2 for the applicable labor category and must obtain the appropriate FAA certifications in accordance with Attachment J-2 Appendix A, Contractor Certification Requirements. The FAA Academy and field facilities have different training needs based on the type of training performed at each location. The FAA Academy provides more generalized initial ATC training as a foundation to newly hired or newly placed developmentals to prepare them for field training. ATC Facilities require location-specific training to certify air traffic specialists at each individual site. The Contractor must support all designated FAA training courses, including specialized staff training courses as identified by the COR. The Contractor must transition to new training materials and

then it must be approved by the FAA. The scope of training support services required at the FAA Academy is defined in the following subparagraphs. The Government may order this support based on the applicable hourly labor rates. C.4.4.1.1 FAA Academy Classroom Training The Contractor must provide FAA-certified instructors, including Lead and Assistant-Lead (A- Lead) Instructors, Adult Educators, and Teaching Assistants, to the FAA Academy at the appropriate date(s), time(s) and location(s) as required by the Government per section C.4.2.5 Training Schedule Coordination, Delivery and Resource Management (also see Attachment J-2 Appendix A, Contractor Certification Requirements). A Lead Instructor teaches the classroom portion of a course and oversees the training that occurs in the lab (if applicable). The Contractor must provide training support, including classroom preparation and instruction, laboratory preparation and instruction, classroom observation (includes observing student activity), and classroom administration. The Contractor must follow instructional program guides, courseware and lesson plan materials, laboratory guidelines, branch directives, and other tools the FAA Academy has been directed to deliver training. C.4.4.1.2 FAA Academy Simulation /

progress report describing the student's performance and identifying the student’s strengths and weaknesses. C.4.4.5 Contractor Certifications FAA certification is required before Instructors, RSOs, RPOs, Lab Managers, TAs, and AEs perform the duties described in Section C.4.3 Management, Supervision and Training Materials Administration. Obtaining certification demonstrates that Contractor employees meet the FAA standards for subject mastery and compliance with FAA policies, orders, practices, and procedures. C.4.4.5.1 Obtaining Certifications The Contractor must follow the certification guidelines outlined in Section J-2, Appendix A for the applicable Labor Category. The Contractor may not perform the duties described in Section C.4.4 Management, Supervision and Training Materials Administration until all applicable certifications have been obtained. The Contractor must utilize the appropriate Government-provided Certification forms to record all employee certifications. All certification forms must be maintained within the CTS II Management Database (CDRL 011), as outlined in Section H.7.2 and be accessible to the COR and CO at all times.
